name: Apple Remote Desktop (ARD)
description: Apple's own macOS fleet management console, sold as a one-time Mac App Store purchase since 2002. Built on an enhanced VNC extension with Apple's own adaptive MVS codec, tuned specifically for managing Macs (software push, remote scripts, inventory) rather than being a general cross-platform remote desktop app.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: ARD doesn't target Linux desktops at all; it's built specifically around macOS management

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: The MVS (Multi-Variant Stream) codec adaptively scales quality, notably optimized for Retina displays

H.264 Codec.comment: Uses Apple's own MVS codec, an enhancement over standard VNC's zlib compression

Wake-on-LAN.comment: A long-standing ARD feature for powering on managed Macs remotely

Pre-Login Access.comment: Can reach the login window via macOS's Remote Management framework

No Account Required.comment: Uses local macOS credentials/Remote Management settings, no Apple ID or cloud account required

KVM Integration.comment: Can manage headless Macs without a physical KVM switch attached, but doesn't integrate with KVM-over-IP devices

2FA / MFA.comment: No dedicated 2FA layer built into ARD itself; security relies on macOS account credentials and AES-128 encryption

Windows: Host.comment: The ARD admin console only runs on macOS

Windows: Client.comment: No official ARD client app for Windows

macOS: Host.comment: The primary and only fully-featured target platform

macOS: Client.comment: The admin console itself is a native macOS app

Linux X11: Host.comment: Reachable only as a basic VNC-compatible target, without ARD's Mac-specific management features

Android: Client.comment: No official ARD app for Android

iOS: Client.comment: No official ARD app for iOS; the admin console is Mac-only

Web Browser: Client.comment: Native macOS app only, no official browser-based access

Apple Silicon GPU (Metal).comment: Not a GPU-benchmarked streaming tool, despite being Apple-Silicon-native software

Free Tier.comment: No free version; no subscription either — it's a flat one-time purchase

Personal: Monthly.comment: One-time purchase model, not a subscription

Enterprise.comment: Single Mac App Store purchase per admin console; can manage an unlimited number of Macs
